newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN RULES-AFL charges Swans defender Dunkley with misconduct
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN RULES-AFL charges Swans defender Dunkley with misconduct

text.p: The Australian Football League (AFL) on Wednesday announced that it had charged Sydney Swans fullback Andrew Dunkley with misconduct over an incident in last Saturday's semifinal against Essendon.
The AFL said it investigated an incident in the first quarter of that match which left Essendon utility player James Hird with a cut under his left eye.
That investigation had been completed and the AFL had decided to charge Dunkley with misconduct "for allegedly striking Hird with a left fist to the head", the statement said.
Dunkley will appear before the AFL Tribunal at 7.30 p.m. on Wednesday.
AFL football operations general manager Ian Collins said statements had been taken from the three field umpires at the match and that television footage had been examined.
Dunkley is due to play his 100th senior AFL game in Saturday's grand final against North Melbourne.
Hird and Brisbane's Michael Voss on Monday were named as joint winners of this year's Brownlow medal for the best and fiarest AFL player.
